title: Lancaster's Borough Road school
summary: Lancaster's Borough Road school used a monitorial method in which older pupils taught younger pupils; it was a specific school implementation of a method distinct from Bell's Madras system.

title: Borough Road College male-apprentice training
wiki: West London Institute of Higher Education
summary: The teacher-training college developed from Lancaster's Borough Road school and records male-apprentice training beginning in 1809, giving the school network a route to prepare teachers.

parents.reason: The college developed from Lancaster's Borough Road school and began training male apprentices in 1809; the school used Lancaster's monitorial method.

title: British and Foreign School Society
summary: Founded in 1808 as the Society for Promoting the Lancasterian System and renamed the British and Foreign School Society in 1814, it organized non-denominational schools using Lancaster's method.

parents.reason: The society was formed to continue Lancaster's lead and promoted his monitorial system through non-denominational British schools.

title: National Society for Education of the Poor
wiki: National Society for Promoting Religious Education
summary: The Church of England's National Society organized schools that used Bell's monitorial system for Anglican education of poor children.

title: French King's Council of State
summary: The French King's Council of State established in 1557 included a judicial section that adjudicated claims against the Crown; the 1799 Conseil d'État was identified as its institutional successor.
